title: Isolation of primary human liver cells from normal and nonalcoholic steatohepatitis livers
author: Liu, Lam, et al.

steps.title: Prepare biosafety cabinet
steps.instruction: Turn on the biological safety cabinet, run it for 10–30 min to purge air, remove all items, and clean interior surfaces with a suitable disinfectant according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Set up pump and water bath
steps.instruction: Place the peristaltic pump and a water bath inside the cabinet, turn on the water bath and heat it to 39 °C.

steps.title: Warm perfusion solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare all perfusion solutions (Buffers A, B, C, D) and place them in the 39 °C water bath for at least 20 min before starting perfusion.

steps.title: Load and prime tubing
steps.instruction: Load sterile perfusion tubing onto the peristaltic pump, place both ends into the Buffer A bottle, turn on the pump and prime the tubing so that solution circulates continuously.

steps.title: Prepare sterile ice field
steps.instruction: In a second biosafety cabinet, cover a pan of ice with a sterile plastic bag, place a sterile field over the ice, and set the liver on this field; arrange a second sterile field with all surgical instruments and supplies.

steps.title: Inspect and trim liver
steps.instruction: Don sterile gloves, pick up the liver, examine for lacerations or bruising, remove the gallbladder with a scalpel if still attached, and excise excess fat, muscle, and diaphragmatic tissue.

steps.title: Resect liver into lobes
steps.instruction: Cut the liver into three pieces: left lobe (for hepatocytes), central lobe (for snap‑frozen tissue/paraffin blocks), and right lobe (for non‑parenchymal cells).

steps.title: Insert perfusion catheters
steps.instruction: Insert barbed catheters into the major portal and/or hepatic vessels without securing them yet.

steps.title: Initial EMEM flush
steps.instruction: Connect a 60 mL syringe filled with cold EMEM to the catheters, flush the liver to identify vessels that give uniform perfusion and to remove residual blood.

steps.title: Secure catheters
steps.instruction: Secure the catheters using 6–7 loose loop stitches around the vessel wall, tighten the suture around the catheter (or barbed luer adaptor), attach the tubing, add additional loops and knots, and seal the cut surface of the liver with size 2‑0 sutures or surgical‑grade glue; close any remaining major vessels with sutures or glue.

steps.title: Leak‑check flush
steps.instruction: Flush the liver again with cold EMEM using the syringe; if any leaks are observed, seal them with glue or additional sutures before proceeding.

steps.title: Weigh liver and start Buffer A perfusion
steps.instruction: Place the liver (still in the catheters) inside a sterile plastic bag, weigh the sealed bag, submerge the bag in the 39 °C water bath, connect to the peristaltic pump set at 20–30 mL/min, and perfuse with Buffer A (EGTA‑containing) for 10–15 min (≈500–600 mL for a left lobe). EGTA chelates calcium to separate cell junctions and clear residual blood.

steps.title: Hepatocyte isolation – Buffer B perfusion
steps.instruction: Perfuse the liver with Buffer B (pronase) for 15–20 min at the same flow rate; stop when the tissue fractures and separates from the capsule.

steps.title: Hepatocyte isolation – tissue dissociation
steps.instruction: Transfer the liver from the bag into a sterile container pre‑warmed (37 °C) DMEM containing 10 % FBS, 25 mM HEPES, 100 nM dexamethasone, 1× ITS, and 1 % Pen/Strep; gently dissect the capsule with sterile scissors or gloved hand to release hepatocytes.

steps.title: Hepatocyte isolation – filtration
steps.instruction: Filter the cell suspension through a three‑layer nylon mesh (500 µm, 250 µm, 85 µm) that has been autoclaved; repeat filtration as needed to maximize cell recovery.

steps.title: Hepatocyte isolation – cell count
steps.instruction: Count cells with a hemocytometer and assess viability using trypan blue.

steps.title: Hepatocyte isolation – low‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Transfer the suspension to 225 mL conical tubes, top with warmed DMEM (same supplements), limit to ≤1 × 10⁹ hepatocytes per tube, and centrifuge at 60–80 g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Hepatocyte isolation – Percoll gradient
steps.instruction: Aspirate supernatant, gently resuspend the pellet in Percoll gradient solution (≈50–100 mL), then centrifuge at 100 g for 10 min at 4 °C with the brake OFF; avoid using a serological pipette, swirl the tube with 50–100 mL media to resuspend.

steps.title: Hepatocyte isolation – wash
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant, wash the pellet in 40 mL pre‑warmed (37 °C) DMEM with the same supplements, centrifuge again at 60–80 g for 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant, and finally resuspend the pellet in a small volume of pre‑warmed DMEM (same supplements).

steps.title: Hepatocyte final check
steps.instruction: Assess final viability and cell number; hepatocytes are now ready for plating or cryopreservation.

steps.title: Non‑parenchymal isolation – Buffer C/D perfusion
steps.instruction: Perfuse the liver sequentially with Buffer C for 15–20 min and then Buffer D for 15–20 min at 20–30 mL/min; stop when the tissue begins to fracture and separate from the capsule. Adjust digestion time to achieve complete but not excessive digestion.

steps.title: Non‑parenchymal isolation – tissue release
steps.instruction: Remove the liver from the bag, place it in a sterile beaker with ice‑cold EMEM, and gently cut with sterile scissors to release cells.

steps.title: Non‑parenchymal isolation – filtration
steps.instruction: Filter the cell suspension through the same three‑layer nylon mesh (500 µm, 250 µm, 85 µm); repeat as needed to maximize recovery.

steps.title: Non‑parenchymal isolation – remove hepatocytes
steps.instruction: Transfer the filtered suspension to 50 mL conical tubes and centrifuge at 60–80 g for 5 min at 4 °C to pellet hepatocytes; keep the supernatant containing NPCs.

steps.title: Non‑parenchymal isolation – NPC pellet
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant, then centrifuge the NPC pellet at 935 g for 8 min at 18 °C to collect total non‑parenchymal cells.

steps.title: Non‑parenchymal isolation – wash and resuspend
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 10 mL EMEM, bring volume to 50 mL with EMEM, and centrifuge again at 700 g for 8 min (18 °C). Discard supernatant.

steps.title: Non‑parenchymal isolation – Nycodenz I preparation
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL GBSS/B to the pellet, then 15 mL Nycodenz I, and bring the total volume to 50 mL with GBSS/B; mix by inversion. Adjust Nycodenz I concentration to 10.4–11 % based on liver fat content.

steps.title: Non‑parenchymal isolation – density gradient layering
steps.instruction: In a 50 mL tube, layer 10 mL Nycodenz II at the bottom, then carefully layer 30 mL of the cell mixture (from previous step) on top, and finally layer 10 mL GBSS/B using a 20 mL syringe with a 19‑gauge needle held against the tube wall; repeat with the remaining 20 mL cell mixture.

steps.title: Non‑parenchymal isolation – gradient centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the layered tubes at 2000 g for 20 min at 4 °C with the brake OFF.

steps.title: Non‑parenchymal isolation – collect HSC layer
steps.instruction: Under the clear GBSS/B layer, a white layer containing hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) appears; collect this layer with a pipette into new 50 mL tubes.

steps.title: Non‑parenchymal isolation – collect LEC/KC layer
steps.instruction: Above the HSC layer, a second layer contains liver endothelial cells (LEC) and myeloid cells (Kupffer cells and bone‑marrow derived myeloid cells); collect this layer for downstream MACS purification (CD11b+ for myeloid, CD146+ then CD31+ for LEC).

steps.title: Non‑parenchymal isolation – wash HSCs
steps.instruction: Add 40 mL GBSS/B to the HSC tube, centrifuge at 935 g for 8 min at 18 °C; repeat wash by centrifuging at 700 g for 8 min at 18 °C.

steps.title: Hepatocyte culture or cryopreservation
steps.instruction: Count hepatocytes, plate at 0.5 × 10⁶ cells /mL on collagen‑coated plates and attach for 2–12 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; then change to pre‑warmed DMEM with 25 mM HEPES, 100 nM dexamethasone, 1× ITS, and 1 % Pen/Strep. For cryopreservation, resuspend cells in CS10 + 100 mM fructose, aliquot 2 mL (≈1.2 × 10⁷ cells) per cryovial, place tubes in a controlled‑rate freezer (4 °C → –90 °C with the programmed steps) and finally store in liquid nitrogen vapor phase.

steps.title: HSC culture or cryopreservation
steps.instruction: Count HSCs, seed 0.5 × 10⁶ cells in DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % amino acids in a 10 cm dish; change media (DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % AA) every 3–4 days until 90 % confluent, then trypsinize, split, or cryopreserve. For freezing, resuspend in CELLBANKER® 1, aliquot 1 mL (≈1 × 10⁶ cells) per tube, use the same controlled‑rate freezer program as for hepatocytes, and store in liquid nitrogen vapor phase.
